scene.label: Act 4, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. A room in Ford's house

lines.text: Mistress Ford, your sorrow hath eaten up my sufferance. I see you are obsequious in your love, and I profess requital to a hair's breadth, not only, Mistress Ford, in the simple office of love, but in all the accoutrement, compliment, and ceremony of it. But are you sure of your husband now?
lines.plainText: Mistress Ford your sorrow hath eaten up my sufferance I see you are obsequious in your love and I profess requital to a hair's breadth not only Mistress Ford in the simple office of love but in all the accoutrement compliment and ceremony of it But are you sure of your husband now

lines.text: He's a-birding, sweet Sir John.
lines.plainText: He's abirding sweet Sir John

lines.text: [Within.] What ho, gossip Ford, what ho!
lines.plainText: Within What ho gossip Ford what ho

lines.text: Step into the chamber, Sir John.
lines.plainText: Step into the chamber Sir John

lines.text: How now, sweetheart, who's at home besides yourself?
lines.plainText: How now sweetheart who's at home besides yourself

lines.text: Why, none but mine own people.
lines.plainText: Why none but mine own people

lines.text: Indeed?
lines.plainText: Indeed

lines.text: No, certainly.
lines.plainText: No certainly

lines.text: [Aside to her.] Speak louder.
lines.plainText: Aside to her Speak louder

lines.text: Truly, I am so glad you have nobody here.
lines.plainText: Truly I am so glad you have nobody here

lines.text: Why?
lines.plainText: Why

lines.text: Why, woman, your husband is in his old lunes again. He so takes on yonder with my husband, so rails against all married mankind, so curses all Eve's daughters, of what complexion soever, and so buffets himself on the forehead, crying "Peer out, peer out!" that any madness I ever yet beheld seemed but tameness, civility, and patience, to this his distemper he is in now. I am glad the fat knight is not here.
lines.plainText: Why woman your husband is in his old lunes again He so takes on yonder with my husband so rails against all married mankind so curses all Eve's daughters of what complexion soever and so buffets himself on the forehead crying Peer out peer out that any madness I ever yet beheld seemed but tameness civility and patience to this his distemper he is in now I am glad the fat knight is not here

lines.text: Why, does he talk of him?
lines.plainText: Why does he talk of him

lines.text: Of none but him, and swears he was carried out, the last time he searched for him, in a basket; protests to my husband he is now here; and hath drawn him and the rest of their company from their sport, to make another experiment of his suspicion. But I am glad the knight is not here. Now he shall see his own foolery.
lines.plainText: Of none but him and swears he was carried out the last time he searched for him in a basket protests to my husband he is now here and hath drawn him and the rest of their company from their sport to make another experiment of his suspicion But I am glad the knight is not here Now he shall see his own foolery

lines.text: How near is he, Mistress Page?
lines.plainText: How near is he Mistress Page

lines.text: Hard by, at street end. He will be here anon.
lines.plainText: Hard by at street end He will be here anon

lines.text: I am undone! The knight is here.
lines.plainText: I am undone The knight is here

lines.text: Why, then, you are utterly shamed, and he's but a dead man. What a woman are you! Away with him, away with him! Better shame than murder.
lines.plainText: Why then you are utterly shamed and he's but a dead man What a woman are you Away with him away with him Better shame than murder

lines.text: Which way should he go? How should I bestow him? Shall I put him into the basket again?
lines.plainText: Which way should he go How should I bestow him Shall I put him into the basket again

lines.text: No, I'll come no more i' the basket. May I not go out ere he come?
lines.plainText: No I'll come no more i' the basket May I not go out ere he come

lines.text: Alas, three of Master Ford's brothers watch the door with pistols, that none shall issue out, otherwise you might slip away ere he came. But what make you here?
lines.plainText: Alas three of Master Ford's brothers watch the door with pistols that none shall issue out otherwise you might slip away ere he came But what make you here

lines.text: What shall I do? I'll creep up into the chimney.
lines.plainText: What shall I do I'll creep up into the chimney

lines.text: There they always use to discharge their birding-pieces.
lines.plainText: There they always use to discharge their birdingpieces

lines.text: Creep into the kiln-hole.
lines.plainText: Creep into the kilnhole

lines.text: Where is it?
lines.plainText: Where is it

lines.text: He will seek there, on my word. Neither press, coffer, chest, trunk, well, vault, but he hath an abstract for the remembrance of such places, and goes to them by his note. There is no hiding you in the house.
lines.plainText: He will seek there on my word Neither press coffer chest trunk well vault but he hath an abstract for the remembrance of such places and goes to them by his note There is no hiding you in the house

lines.text: I'll go out then.
lines.plainText: I'll go out then

lines.text: If you go out in your own semblance, you die, Sir John—unless you go out disguised.
lines.plainText: If you go out in your own semblance you die Sir Johnunless you go out disguised

lines.text: How might we disguise him?
lines.plainText: How might we disguise him

lines.text: Alas the day, I know not. There is no woman's gown big enough for him; otherwise he might put on a hat, a muffler, and a kerchief, and so escape.
lines.plainText: Alas the day I know not There is no woman's gown big enough for him otherwise he might put on a hat a muffler and a kerchief and so escape

lines.text: Good hearts, devise something. Any extremity rather than a mischief.
lines.plainText: Good hearts devise something Any extremity rather than a mischief

lines.text: My maid's aunt, the fat woman of Brentford, has a gown above.
lines.plainText: My maid's aunt the fat woman of Brentford has a gown above

lines.text: On my word, it will serve him. She's as big as he is. And there's her thrummed hat, and her muffler too.—Run up, Sir John.
lines.plainText: On my word it will serve him She's as big as he is And there's her thrummed hat and her muffler tooRun up Sir John

lines.text: Go, go, sweet Sir John. Mistress Page and I will look some linen for your head.
lines.plainText: Go go sweet Sir John Mistress Page and I will look some linen for your head

lines.text: Quick, quick! We'll come dress you straight; put on the gown the while.
lines.plainText: Quick quick We'll come dress you straight put on the gown the while

lines.text: I would my husband would meet him in this shape. He cannot abide the old woman of Brentford; he swears she's a witch, forbade her my house, and hath threatened to beat her.
lines.plainText: I would my husband would meet him in this shape He cannot abide the old woman of Brentford he swears she's a witch forbade her my house and hath threatened to beat her

lines.text: Heaven guide him to thy husband's cudgel and the devil guide his cudgel afterwards!
lines.plainText: Heaven guide him to thy husband's cudgel and the devil guide his cudgel afterwards

lines.text: But is my husband coming?
lines.plainText: But is my husband coming

lines.text: Ay, in good sadness is he, and talks of the basket too, howsoever he hath had intelligence.
lines.plainText: Ay in good sadness is he and talks of the basket too howsoever he hath had intelligence

lines.text: We'll try that; for I'll appoint my men to carry the basket again, to meet him at the door with it as they did last time.
lines.plainText: We'll try that for I'll appoint my men to carry the basket again to meet him at the door with it as they did last time

lines.text: Nay, but he'll be here presently. Let's go dress him like the witch of Brentford.
lines.plainText: Nay but he'll be here presently Let's go dress him like the witch of Brentford

lines.text: I'll first direct my men what they shall do with the basket. Go up, I'll bring linen for him straight.
lines.plainText: I'll first direct my men what they shall do with the basket Go up I'll bring linen for him straight

lines.text: Hang him, dishonest varlet! We cannot misuse him enough.
lines.plainText: Hang him dishonest varlet We cannot misuse him enough

lines.text: We'll leave a proof, by that which we will do,
lines.plainText: We'll leave a proof by that which we will do

lines.text: Wives may be merry and yet honest too.
lines.plainText: Wives may be merry and yet honest too

lines.text: We do not act that often jest and laugh;
lines.plainText: We do not act that often jest and laugh

lines.text: 'Tis old but true: "Still swine eats all the draff."
lines.plainText: 'Tis old but true Still swine eats all the draff

content.text: Enter Mistress Ford with John and Robert.

lines.text: Go, sirs, take the basket again on your shoulders. Your master is hard at door; if he bid you set it down, obey him. Quickly, dispatch.
lines.plainText: Go sirs take the basket again on your shoulders Your master is hard at door if he bid you set it down obey him Quickly dispatch

lines.text: Come, come, take it up.
lines.plainText: Come come take it up

lines.text: Pray heaven it be not full of knight again.
lines.plainText: Pray heaven it be not full of knight again

lines.text: I hope not, I had lief as bear so much lead.
lines.plainText: I hope not I had lief as bear so much lead

content.text: Enter Ford, Page, Shallow, Caius and Sir Hugh Evans.

lines.text: Ay, but if it prove true, Master Page, have you any way then to unfool me again?—Set down the basket, villain! Somebody call my wife. Youth in a basket! O you panderly rascals! There's a knot, a gin, a pack, a conspiracy against me. Now shall the devil be shamed.—What, wife, I say! Come, come forth! Behold what honest clothes you send forth to bleaching!
lines.plainText: Ay but if it prove true Master Page have you any way then to unfool me againSet down the basket villain Somebody call my wife Youth in a basket O you panderly rascals There's a knot a gin a pack a conspiracy against me Now shall the devil be shamedWhat wife I say Come come forth Behold what honest clothes you send forth to bleaching

lines.text: Why, this passes, Master Ford! You are not to go loose any longer; you must be pinioned.
lines.plainText: Why this passes Master Ford You are not to go loose any longer you must be pinioned

lines.text: Why, this is lunatics, this is mad as a mad dog.
lines.plainText: Why this is lunatics this is mad as a mad dog

lines.text: Indeed, Master Ford, this is not well, indeed.
lines.plainText: Indeed Master Ford this is not well indeed

lines.text: So say I too, sir.
lines.plainText: So say I too sir

lines.text: Heaven be my witness you do, if you suspect me in any dishonesty.
lines.plainText: Heaven be my witness you do if you suspect me in any dishonesty

lines.text: Well said, brazen-face, hold it out.—Come forth, sirrah.
lines.plainText: Well said brazenface hold it outCome forth sirrah

lines.text: This passes.
lines.plainText: This passes

lines.text: Are you not ashamed? Let the clothes alone.
lines.plainText: Are you not ashamed Let the clothes alone

lines.text: I shall find you anon.
lines.plainText: I shall find you anon

lines.text: 'Tis unreasonable. Will you take up your wife's clothes? Come, away.
lines.plainText: 'Tis unreasonable Will you take up your wife's clothes Come away

lines.text: Empty the basket, I say.
lines.plainText: Empty the basket I say

lines.text: Why, man, why?
lines.plainText: Why man why

lines.text: Master Page, as I am a man, there was one conveyed out of my house yesterday in this basket. Why may not he be there again? In my house I am sure he is. My intelligence is true, my jealousy is reasonable.—Pluck me out all the linen.
lines.plainText: Master Page as I am a man there was one conveyed out of my house yesterday in this basket Why may not he be there again In my house I am sure he is My intelligence is true my jealousy is reasonablePluck me out all the linen

lines.text: If you find a man there, he shall die a flea's death.
lines.plainText: If you find a man there he shall die a flea's death

lines.text: Here's no man.
lines.plainText: Here's no man

lines.text: By my fidelity, this is not well, Master Ford, this wrongs you.
lines.plainText: By my fidelity this is not well Master Ford this wrongs you

lines.text: Master Ford, you must pray, and not follow the imaginations of your own heart. This is jealousies.
lines.plainText: Master Ford you must pray and not follow the imaginations of your own heart This is jealousies

lines.text: Well, he's not here I seek for.
lines.plainText: Well he's not here I seek for

lines.text: No, nor nowhere else but in your brain.
lines.plainText: No nor nowhere else but in your brain

lines.text: Help to search my house this one time. If I find not what I seek, show no colour for my extremity, let me for ever be your table-sport. Let them say of me "As jealous as Ford, that searched a hollow walnut for his wife's leman." Satisfy me once more, once more search with me.
lines.plainText: Help to search my house this one time If I find not what I seek show no colour for my extremity let me for ever be your tablesport Let them say of me As jealous as Ford that searched a hollow walnut for his wife's leman Satisfy me once more once more search with me

content.text: [Exeunt John and Robert with the basket.]

lines.text: What, ho, Mistress Page! Come you and the old woman down; my husband will come into the chamber.
lines.plainText: What ho Mistress Page Come you and the old woman down my husband will come into the chamber

lines.text: Old woman? What old woman's that?
lines.plainText: Old woman What old woman's that

lines.text: Why, it is my maid's aunt of Brentford.
lines.plainText: Why it is my maid's aunt of Brentford

lines.text: A witch, a quean, an old cozening quean! Have I not forbid her my house? She comes of errands, does she? We are simple men; we do not know what's brought to pass under the profession of fortune-telling. She works by charms, by spells, by the figure, and such daubery as this is, beyond our element. We know nothing.—Come down, you witch, you hag, you! Come down, I say!
lines.plainText: A witch a quean an old cozening quean Have I not forbid her my house She comes of errands does she We are simple men we do not know what's brought to pass under the profession of fortunetelling She works by charms by spells by the figure and such daubery as this is beyond our element We know nothingCome down you witch you hag you Come down I say

lines.text: Nay, good sweet husband!—Good gentlemen, let him not strike the old woman.
lines.plainText: Nay good sweet husbandGood gentlemen let him not strike the old woman

content.text: Enter Falstaff disguised as an old woman, led by Mistress Page.

lines.text: Come, Mother Prat; come, give me your hand.
lines.plainText: Come Mother Prat come give me your hand

lines.text: I'll prat her. [Beats him.] Out of my door, you witch, you rag, you baggage, you polecat, you runnion! Out, out! I'll conjure you, I'll fortune-tell you.
lines.plainText: I'll prat her Beats him Out of my door you witch you rag you baggage you polecat you runnion Out out I'll conjure you I'll fortunetell you

lines.text: Are you not ashamed? I think you have killed the poor woman.
lines.plainText: Are you not ashamed I think you have killed the poor woman

lines.text: Nay, he will do it. 'Tis a goodly credit for you.
lines.plainText: Nay he will do it 'Tis a goodly credit for you

lines.text: Hang her, witch!
lines.plainText: Hang her witch

lines.text: By yea and no, I think the 'oman is a witch indeed. I like not when a 'oman has a great peard. I spy a great peard under her muffler.
lines.plainText: By yea and no I think the 'oman is a witch indeed I like not when a 'oman has a great peard I spy a great peard under her muffler

lines.text: Will you follow, gentlemen? I beseech you follow, see but the issue of my jealousy. If I cry out thus upon no trail, never trust me when I open again.
lines.plainText: Will you follow gentlemen I beseech you follow see but the issue of my jealousy If I cry out thus upon no trail never trust me when I open again

lines.text: Let's obey his humour a little further. Come, gentlemen.
lines.plainText: Let's obey his humour a little further Come gentlemen

content.text: [Exeunt Ford, Page, Caius, Evans and Shallow.]

lines.text: Trust me, he beat him most pitifully.
lines.plainText: Trust me he beat him most pitifully

lines.text: Nay, by th' mass, that he did not; he beat him most unpitifully, methought.
lines.plainText: Nay by th' mass that he did not he beat him most unpitifully methought

lines.text: I'll have the cudgel hallowed and hung o'er the altar. It hath done meritorious service.
lines.plainText: I'll have the cudgel hallowed and hung o'er the altar It hath done meritorious service

lines.text: What think you? May we, with the warrant of womanhood and the witness of a good conscience, pursue him with any further revenge?
lines.plainText: What think you May we with the warrant of womanhood and the witness of a good conscience pursue him with any further revenge

lines.text: The spirit of wantonness is sure scared out of him. If the devil have him not in fee-simple, with fine and recovery, he will never, I think, in the way of waste, attempt us again.
lines.plainText: The spirit of wantonness is sure scared out of him If the devil have him not in feesimple with fine and recovery he will never I think in the way of waste attempt us again

lines.text: Shall we tell our husbands how we have served him?
lines.plainText: Shall we tell our husbands how we have served him

lines.text: Yes, by all means, if it be but to scrape the figures out of your husband's brains. If they can find in their hearts the poor unvirtuous fat knight shall be any further afflicted, we two will still be the ministers.
lines.plainText: Yes by all means if it be but to scrape the figures out of your husband's brains If they can find in their hearts the poor unvirtuous fat knight shall be any further afflicted we two will still be the ministers

lines.text: I'll warrant they'll have him publicly shamed, and methinks there would be no period to the jest should he not be publicly shamed.
lines.plainText: I'll warrant they'll have him publicly shamed and methinks there would be no period to the jest should he not be publicly shamed

lines.text: Come, to the forge with it, then shape it. I would not have things cool.
